title: Finite constant-extension datum, base change and geometric-fibre identification
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and an integer $m\ge1$. Write $k_m\subset k$ for its specified subfield of cardinality $q^m$ and $i_m:k_0\to k_m$ for its specified inclusion. The constant-extension datum is $D_m=(p,am,q^m,k_m,k)$, with the same fixed algebraic closure and its subfield inclusion. For a $k_0$-scheme $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], define the constant-extension model $X_{0,m}=X_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_0}\operatorname{Spec}k_m$ [def-pc-fibre-product], as a $k_m$-scheme via its second projection. The original-base model is the same scheme with structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ obtained by composing with $\operatorname{Spec}(i_m)$, and $g_m$ is its first projection to $X_0$. If $X_0$ is moreover separated, as in the existing constructions, then, using the inclusion $k_m\subset k$, the distinguished sheet is the map $X_{0,m}\times_{k_m}k\to X_{0,m}\times_{k_0}k$ determined by the two pullback projections. The canonical geometric-fibre isomorphism $X_{0,m}\times_{k_m}k\simeq X_0\times_{k_0}k$ is the composite of this sheet map and the geometric base change $g_m\times_{k_0}k$ of $g_m$ [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category], equivalently the associativity isomorphism of these fibre products. For a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and any finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, the heart-forgetful functor from its common-stage constructible Weil sheaves [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] [def-weil-constructible-heart] to the common-stage constructible category on $Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ sends each heart object $(M,\theta)$ to $M$ and every morphism to its underlying carrier morphism.
